_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Naval Aviation Cyber Table Top (CTT) Report Template
summary: This Data Item Description contains the format and content for the contractor to report results of the Cyber Table Top (CTT) analysis.

preparation_instructions.title: Content.
preparation_instructions.content: The report shall contain the following information and be submitted in the format specified below. This will allow ease of integration with other cyber table top assessments performed in relation to this effort. Each paragraph includes a description of the expected content associated with that particular paragraph. The contractor shall pay close attention to the classification of this analysis and mark the deliverable in accordance with the security marking requirements of the contract.

children.title: Executive Summary.
children.content: Summarize the entire study. Include the purpose for the study, the team members and their roles, the scope of the study, and the study timeframe. Include any rationale for approved (Specify Government POC) tailoring or deviations from the SWP and Table Top Assessment Process. The major findings of the study will likely be classified at the SECRET or higher level, so the findings should only be included if the report is appropriately classified. Also include any considerations, difficulties, compromises, or assumptions that may have significantly impacted the output of the assessment. Finally, include a high-level discussion on the recommendations and mitigation strategies. Ensure portion markings are maintained, especially if an UNCLASSIFIED subset of the Executive Summary is needed for communications at that level. This summary should not be longer than two pages in length.

children.title: System Information.
children.content: This is the formal introduction to the Cyber Table Top (CTT) task at hand. The introduction should contain the following information:

children.title: A description of the system under review.
The system's current position in the acquisition lifecycle.
The overall reasons behind conducting a CTT in general.
System boundaries included with the scope of the CTT.
Results from previous cyber security assessments (if any) that were used to inform this assessment.
Recommendations or lessons learned specific to the system under study that will inform upcoming system CTT/Cyber Risk Assessment (CRA), or SETR events.
Specific threats included in the CTT and those that are deemed out of scope for the effort
CTT Report information.
